models.name: DXP480T Plus

leds.note: Only the power LED works; the model has no drive bays. A 5.5.0 owner (#271) reports the LEDs do not work there: LED probe failed, 0 LEDs; the power LED blinks white at power-on.

fans.note: UGREEN's fan driver expects cpu on header 3 and case fans on headers 2 and 4; header 4 is unconfirmed, so there is no fan control.

case.note: Drawn after UGREEN's manual (front, rear ports, four M.2 slots 01 to 04, two SO-DIMM sockets); which SSD sits in which slot is assumed from the PCIe order. Works on 5.5.0 (#271): no bays, one LAN port and the M.2 drives are listed; the diag found five NVMe drives where the registry has four slots, all shown as plain m2, so the slot order is still unconfirmed.

sensors.note: Reported working by an owner on 5.5.0 (#271): CPU temperature check ok (coretemp 55 C), NVMe temperatures read.

panel.note: An owner on 5.5.0 (#271) ticked the front panel as working. The diag reads real pad registers (power 0xFD6E0810 = 0x44000100, reset 0xFD6E0770 = 0x44000102) and both buttons read released; a panel buttons --watch test is still open.

models.note: All-flash model: no SATA bays, four M.2 slots (shown as drives in the case view), one 10G LAN port. Only the power LED works.

models.name: DXP2800

watchdog.note: Expected, from the vendor driver and the kernel it87_wdt: the plugin only feeds a timer it sees counting, never arms it, and yields to it87_wdt. Not confirmed on this hardware.

leds.note: Reported working by users. SUB2 boards (BIOS EM_DXP2800S_SUB2_V1.0.11) only: the LED MCU sits behind Intel LPSS I2C1 and works by default (5.5.0-next.000133, 2026-11-07, DanielRuppen, #214; lpss_leds="0" turns it off); bay order confirmed with Identify, reboot confirmed (#214). Boards from December 2025 (V1.2, rev 251215) use LED chip 0xc5b2, which ignores the DX/DXP write frame (miskcoo issue 128). The driver UGREEN ships serves this model with the frame without LED ID, so the plugin tries that frame when the first one is not acknowledged. An owner confirmed the LEDs of a V1.2 board with miskcoo's tool and that SMBus block frame (issue 128; his README marks V1.2 experimental); not yet run with this plugin.

fans.note: Reported working by a user on a SUB2 board (5.5.0-next.000133, 2026-11-07, #244): IT8613 found, fan headers and spinning fans checked ok. Same IT8613E as the DXP6800 Pro, header wiring not known: the fan probe finds which output drives which fan and fan control stays off until you confirm its result. One fan was reported on tach 3 (1726 rpm), none on tach 2; UGREEN's own driver also drives only header 3.

case.note: Reported working by a user on a SUB2 board (5.5.0-next.000133, 2026-11-07, #244): bays, M.2 slots and LAN ports checked ok. Drawn after UGREEN's manual and photos (front, rear with 12V inlet, two M.2 slots on the inner left wall of the cage); one SO-DIMM socket in the bottom panel.

sensors.note: Reported working by a user on a SUB2 board (5.5.0-next.000133, 2026-11-07, #244): CPU temperature checked ok.

models.note: Two bays, two M.2 slots, one 2.5G LAN port. The V1.2 board (December 2025) has a new LED chip: the plugin falls back to the frame UGREEN ships for it, confirmed on a V1.2 board with miskcoo's tool, not yet with this plugin. SUB2 boards (BIOS EM_DXP2800S_SUB2) put the LED controller behind an Intel I2C controller without a kernel driver: the plugin drives them by default (lpss_leds="0" in leds.cfg turns that off); LEDs confirmed on a SUB2 board (#214), bay order right, reboot confirmed; ugreen-led-i2c lpss-probe checks the board without changing an LED.

models.name: DXP2800 GT

leds.note: AMD DesignWare I2C controller like the DXP4800 GT, no Intel SMBus; miskcoo's driver for it is work in progress (issues 122, 123). Other tools control all LEDs after the boot-finish write of 1 to 0x20005440 (issue 123), a user reports a month on TrueNAS; our CS201x path does the same write but nobody has run it. Bay order guessed.

fans.note: Fan control stays off until you run `/usr/local/emhttp/plugins/ugreen-nas-control/backend/ugreen-nas-fan cs201x confirm`. A community tester (2026-10-31, next channel) saw both fans follow the modes and a custom curve, 1834 rpm (CPU) and 603 rpm (case) at 25 %, and the BIOS speed (about 60 %) back after removing the plugin. Registers and fan roles are from UGREEN's own CS201x driver. 25 % floor, stall point not measured.

case.note: Inside after UGREEN's manual; slot numbering assumed. Front and rear after the product photos, not compared on a device.

panel.note: Buttons from UGREEN's driver source; the vendor driver has no beeper for this model.

models.note: Two bays (U.2 capable), two M.2 slots, one 10G LAN port. LEDs are enabled but nobody has confirmed them. Case view (front and rear after the product photos, inside after the UGREEN manual); fan control after `/usr/local/emhttp/plugins/ugreen-nas-control/backend/ugreen-nas-fan cs201x confirm` (Chipsea CS201x embedded controller; wiring from the UGREEN driver, confirmed on a device by a community tester).

models.name: DXP4800 Plus / Pro

watchdog.note: Expected, from the vendor driver and the kernel it87_wdt: the plugin only feeds a timer it sees counting, never arms it, and yields to it87_wdt. Not confirmed on this hardware.

leds.note: Reported working by users of the Plus and the Pro (miskcoo issue 121), and by a Plus owner on 5.5.0 (#266): LED probe ok at 0x3a, 6 LEDs.

fans.note: Reported working by a Plus owner on 5.5.0 (#266): IT8613 found, fan headers and spinning fans checked ok. Same IT8613E as the DXP6800 Pro, header wiring not known: the fan probe finds which output drives which fan and fan control stays off until you confirm its result. The Plus was reported to use outputs 2 and 3; UGREEN's own driver expects cpu on header 2 and case on header 3.

case.note: Front and rear confirmed by a Plus owner. The two M.2 slots of the underside panel are printed M2-KEYM1 (next to the RAM) and M2-KEYM3 on the board, shown as M.2-1 and M.2-3 (UGREEN's photos agree); the third slot, M2-KEYM2, is inside the case. Inside view otherwise after UGREEN's manual, the Pro was not compared. Works on 5.5.0 too (#266).

sensors.note: Not confirmed. A Plus owner reported the ACPI thermal zone as a fixed value of about 28 C (5.5.0, #266). It is a BIOS constant, not a mainboard reading, and is no longer shown as the mainboard temperature.

panel.note: Beeper: confirmed by a Plus owner. Buttons: the pad registers read real values (power 0xFD6A0980 = 0x04000100, reset 0xFD6D0A10 = 0x84000102). panel buttons --watch saw the reset button (down and up, held 0.60 s) but never the power button. The power button does start the box from off, so it may reach Linux as an ACPI power-button event instead of through this pad; not checked yet.

models.note: Four bays, two M.2 slots, one 10G and one 2.5G LAN port. Fan control after a fan probe.

models.name: DXP8800 Plus

watchdog.note: Expected, from the vendor driver and the kernel it87_wdt: the plugin only feeds a timer it sees counting, never arms it, and yields to it87_wdt. Not confirmed on this hardware.

leds.note: LED protocol verified on this model by miskcoo's driver, confirmed by users of this plugin.

fans.note: Fan probe found cpu on pwm2 and the case fans on pwm3 and pwm4; fan control with custom curves confirmed by a user. On 5.2.0 header 4 (pwm4) stayed in automatic mode in the diag. Control register 0x1e of UGREEN's driver confirmed on 5.5.0-next.000133 (2026-11-07, #165): after a restart fan4 ran manual (48 %, 901 rpm, 0x1e = 0x08, bit 7 clear), where 5.4.0 showed it automatic at about 1061 rpm.

panel.note: Buttons: the pad registers read 0x84000100 (power) and 0x84000102 (reset), and panel buttons --watch showed power down, press and up and reset down and up. Beeper: the beeper test sounded right after the click. On some boots the BIOS hides the pad registers (0xFF).

models.name: iDX6011 / iDX6012 / Pro

watchdog.note: iDX6011 Pro only, same register map as the DXP4800 GT, not confirmed there. Never the plain iDX6011 or the iDX6012: 0x98/0x99 is a fan tachometer.

leds.note: Bay order (Pro: bays 3-4 on the Intel controller, plain iDX6011 and iDX6012: bays 5-6) follows the MIT-licensed plugins noodlemctwoodle/unraid-ugreen-idx6011-pro and omgapuppy/unraid-ugreen-idx6011-led-fan; not checked on a device with this plugin, use Identify to confirm. LED chip 0xc5b2. The Pro has a second LAN LED (register 2, `netdev2` in ugreen-led-i2c, from the driver UGREEN ships); the plugin pages do not show it yet.

fans.note: Pro only: it uses the same IT5571 embedded controller as the DXP4800 GT with four fans (second CPU fan, second case fan; their registers are from the MIT-licensed noodlemctwoodle plugin), a 25 % floor because the case fan stalls near 20 %, and emergency limits of 88 C CPU and 60 C disk. Not run on a device with this plugin. The plain iDX6011 and iDX6012 have a different fan map: the plugin shows their fan readings (speed, duty, mode) and writes nothing. The Pro LCD backlight can be read and set.

case.note: Drawn after photos, inside after UGREEN's manual; slot numbering assumed. Not compared on a device. The iDX6012 is the pre-launch name of the iDX6011 as far as known.

models.note: Six bays, two M.2 slots, a display at the front (Pro: 3.7 inch LCD), two 10G LAN ports, two Thunderbolt 4 ports, OCuLink. Fan control on the Pro only; the plain iDX6011 and iDX6012 show fan readings only (read-only).
